title: Reform UK Aides Suspended After Channel 4 Sting Alleges Scheme to Bypass Foreign Donation Ban
detail: Two of Nigel Farage's most senior Reform UK aides — chief of staff Dan Jukes and head of policy James Orr — stood down on 4 September 2026, hours after Channel 4 News broadcast an undercover investigation, produced with the group Verbatim, in which the pair were secretly filmed discussing how a fictional wealthy American could route donations to the party despite UK law banning foreign political funding, including a proposed £500,000 gift channelled through the donor's UK-resident son and over £30,000 to cover Reform-commissioned opinion polling. The revelations broke as Farage opened Reform's annual conference in Birmingham, and the party was reported to the Metropolitan Police and the Electoral Commission. Farage dismissed the recorded remarks as "boasts" and "loose talk" and insisted Reform had "not taken any dodgy money," while the party separately called the documentary "a hoax perpetuated by foreign-funded, climate change activists." It compounds a separate parliamentary standards probe into a £5 million gift Farage received from crypto entrepreneur Christopher Harborne, which he says was intended for personal security and predated his election as an MP.

media.caption: Reform UK was reported to police and the Electoral Commission after a Channel 4 sting alleged a scheme to bypass the foreign donations ban
